papers.title: NVIDIA-labs OO Agents: Native Python Object-Oriented Agents
claims: NOOA models an agent as a native Python object whose methods are actions, fields are state, docstrings act as prompts, and type annotations serve as contracts.
Deterministic Python methods and LLM-completed methods share the same object interface, making agent behavior easier to test, trace, refactor, and improve as software.
The framework combines typed input/output, live object references, code-as-action, explicit object state, programmable loop engineering, and harness APIs for context and events on one surface.
papers.why_it_matters: Grounds Frankie's object-like typed state, deterministic safety kernel, model-facing methods, and the separation between deterministic guards and model-completed behavior.

papers.title: ACM: Agentic Context Management for Long Horizon Tasks
claims: ACM gives an agent explicit context-editing tools instead of relying only on rigid heuristic compression.
The agent can decide when to compress context, offload discarded content to external memory, and retrieve it later on demand.
The paper reports that active context management reduces peak token pressure and improves consistency across independent long-horizon trials.
papers.why_it_matters: Grounds explicit long-horizon recall/offload methods, named durable external memory, and an explicit working set for Frankie's live-session context.

papers.title: Kernel Forge: An Agent Harness for LLM-based Generation and Optimization of CUDA Kernels
claims: Kernel Forge is an end-to-end agentic harness that operates on unmodified PyTorch models and includes monitoring and debugging of candidate outputs.
Its search uses Monte Carlo Tree Search to explore multiple optimization paths rather than a single linear refinement chain.
The system evaluates candidate kernel changes empirically and reports performance improvements across multiple model workloads.
papers.why_it_matters: Provides a precedent for Frankie's improvement search being multi-path, instrumented, empirically validated, and separable from production application rather than a single self-editing chain.

papers.title: Agentic Context Management: Solving Agent Memory and Cost by Treating Them as Lifecycle and Architecture Problems
claims: The paper frames agent context management as a lifecycle and architecture problem rather than only a storage-and-retrieval problem.
It decomposes the lifecycle into architecting, ingesting, scoping, anticipating, and compacting/consolidation.
It argues that validated compaction is required to control long-horizon context cost while preserving decision-relevant fidelity and provenance.
papers.why_it_matters: Grounds Frankie's separation of immutable evidence, scoped working context, provenance-preserving memory, anticipation of future dependencies, and explicit compaction/reflection stages.

papers.title: Self-Improvements in Modern Agentic Systems: A Survey
claims: The survey represents a modern agent as a foundation model coupled to an operational scaffold of prompts, memory, tools, and control logic.
It formalizes self-improvement as a self-induced update operator that obtains and commits updates to model parameters or scaffold components.
It organizes prior work by what is updated and by the signal that drives the update, providing a systems taxonomy for controlled agent evolution.
papers.why_it_matters: Provides Frankie's explicit mutable-surface taxonomy so strategy, skills, playbooks, prompts, retrieval, tools, data contracts, tests, and release state are versioned rather than treated as one opaque prompt.

papers.title: Adaptive Auto-Harness: Sustained Self-Improvement for Agentic System Deployment on Open-Ended Task Streams
claims: Open-ended task streams make one densely and repeatedly updated harness brittle because task distributions shift and heterogeneous tasks need different harnesses.
Adaptive Auto-Harness uses a stateful multi-agent evolver, a harness tree with solve-time routing, and human-steering hooks when history lacks the needed signal.
The system is evaluated on prediction-market, security-competition, and event-forecasting streams.
papers.why_it_matters: Directly supports a Frankie harness tree with explicit task routes instead of one universal self-modifying harness, and it supports human steering for novel market regimes.

papers.title: Recursive Self-Evolving Agents via Held-Out Selection
claims: RSEA carries a compact three-layer natural-language state consisting of an imperative strategy, reusable skills, and a procedural playbook.
It rewrites those layers from its own trajectories but commits a candidate only if it does not regress on a disjoint held-out split using a strict keep-better gate.
The paper reports that unguarded context evolution can be high variance and that strict held-out selection is the mechanism used to prevent regression.
papers.why_it_matters: Grounds Frankie's strategy/skills/playbook harness state and a precommitted held-out keep-better gate before any candidate can become release-eligible.

papers.title: MOSS: Self-Evolution through Source-Level Rewriting in Autonomous Agent Systems
claims: MOSS argues that text-only mutation cannot reach structural failures in routing, hook ordering, state invariants, and dispatch that live in source code.
Its source-level evolution is anchored to curated production-failure evidence and runs through a deterministic multi-stage pipeline.
Candidate code is verified by replay in ephemeral trial workers before a user-consent-gated promotion with health-probe rollback.
papers.why_it_matters: Frankie may propose source-level research-harness changes, but only as isolated trial-worker candidates. Production application remains outside Frankie and requires explicit human-reviewed release.

papers.title: AgentDevel: Reframing Self-Evolving LLM Agents as Release Engineering
claims: AgentDevel externalizes self-improvement into a regression-aware release pipeline rather than embedding unrestricted self-refinement inside the agent.
It uses an implementation-blind critic, script-based executable diagnosis, and flip-centered gating that treats pass-to-fail regressions and fail-to-pass fixes as first-class evidence.
It maintains a single canonical version line and emphasizes non-regression and auditable release artifacts.
papers.why_it_matters: Grounds Frankie's single canonical release lineage, symptom-level diagnosis, explicit pass-to-fail regression accounting, and separation of candidate generation from release authority.

papers.title: EvoHarness-RL: Learning Self-Evolving Runtime Harness for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
claims: EvoHarness-RL exposes Belief, Progress, and Experience as policy-facing external harness state rather than one undifferentiated memory store.
It gives the policy explicit external-state actions and uses cost-aware reinforcement learning to make state access selective rather than automatic.

Its reported training dynamics include harness annealing, where external-state calls become more selective, and harness evolution, where progress and experience are consolidated into a compact task-adaptive substrate.
papers.why_it_matters: Frankie already has the needed state organs, so the paper is integrated as a taxonomy and access-policy layer rather than a rebuild: Belief maps to causal decision state, Progress to A-68 lens books, Experience to A-62 track records/play retrieval/reviewed lessons; track/commit/recall/note access is instrumented and costed, while NOVA compaction remains conservative and A-65-gated before any lossy view becomes decision-bearing.
